Mobile Produce Markets

We’re excited to welcome back Mobile Produce Markets participants this April! Reusable grocery bags are restocked and will be provided for all participants, while supplies last. The modified 2025 schedule is listed below:

  • First Thursday: Barack, Glenwood, Sullivant Gardens
  • First Friday: Marion Franklin, Scioto Southland
  • Second Thursday: Dodge, Holton
  • Second Friday: Barnett, Far East
  • Third Thursday: Linden, Tuttle
  • Third Friday: Adams, Douglas (replacing Beatty)
  • Fourth Friday: Feddersen, Howard

FreshTrak Training

There have been minor changes to the intake process. Photo ID is no longer required. To refresh yourself on how to do intakes, please mark your calendars and plan to attend a virtual FreshTrak training session on Thursday, March 13 at 10 a.m. Make sure you register using the training registration link

Go, Lunch! SUN Meals Update

Applications for the Go, Lunch! Summer Food Service Program are now open and will close on March 28. We encourage all CRPD locations participating in the program to complete their application promptly. Each participating site must have at least two trained site supervisors. Stay tuned for more information on site supervisor training sessions coming soon.

Walk With a Doc Kick-Off

Walk With a Doc will return April 5! Join us at Woodward Community Center or Marion Franklin Community Center from 9-10 a.m. for a brisk morning walk with a local medical provider. During each Walk With a Doc session, you will learn about various health topics from a local healthcare professional, meet new people, enjoy a walk at your own pace, and have a chance to earn prizes - all for free!

Participants who attend five or more walks will earn a free t-shirt! Walk With a Doc sessions will take place every Saturday at our parks across the city following the schedule below:

  • First and Third Saturday: Woodward Park, Marion Franklin
  • Second and Fourth Saturday: Dodge Park, Far East
  • Third Saturday: Linden, Tuttle
  • Fourth Saturday: Dodge, Holton
  • Second Friday: Barnett, Far East
  • Third Saturday: Linden, Tuttle

The end of year celebration will be held on Saturday, Nov. 1, at Franklin Park. Make sure you're there!

Mobile Produce Markets

Produce Market Surveys: This is the final month for the mobile produce markets. We want to extend our gratitude for yet another successful year. The 2025 produce season will begin in April. Information will be posted to the public when the dates are final. As a reminder, we have developed a brief survey for community members to complete at the produce markets. This data will be invaluable in improving our services. The food office is still administering the survey at the mobile produce markets, but you are also welcome to help us collect data. You can access the survey here.

Senior Boxes: As a reminder, the Mid-Ohio Food Collective Senior Box program is now exclusively referral-based . Eligible seniors can sign up to have a box of nonperishable food delivered to their homes. To receive the referral link to the CFSP referral program, you need to complete the training first. Link to training can be found here. The remaining training sessions are listed below:

  • Thursday, Nov. 14 | 10:00-10:30 a.m.
  • Wednesday, Nov. 20 | 2:30-3:00 p.m.

Fun Food Recipe: Carver Dip

Ingredients

Directions

  • One 12-16 ounces can of sweet potatoes

1. Drain the liquid off the sweet potatoes
  • ½ cup of unsweetened applesauce

2. Combine all ingredients in a microwave safe bowl
  • ¼ teaspoon of cinnamon

3. Cook in a microwave for 1.5 minutes (90 seconds) or until heated through
  • 1 teaspoon of sugar

4. Stir until smooth

 

Makes eight servings

Cost/serving: $0.15

Serving size: ¼ cup

TIP: This can be served hot or cold. Serve as a spread or dip for graham crackers or fruit.

Mobile Produce Markets

Produce Market Surveys:We want to express our gratitude to all recreation staff and volunteers for facilitating successful produce market events for our community.

As we approach the end of this year's Mobile Produce Market, we are eager to gather feedback to enhance our future initiatives. We have developed a brief survey for community members to complete at the produce markets. This data will be invaluable in improving our services. The food office will administer the survey at the mobile produce markets, but you are also welcome to help us collect data.  You can access the survey HERE.

Remaining Produce Markets for 2024: Please note that while we have two more months of markets left, the fourth week of November will not feature any markets.

Produce Bags: A limited supply of cloth produce bags is still available for our participants. Those with bags are encouraged to bring them to future markets to help conserve resources.

The Mid-Ohio Food Collective Senior Box program is now exclusively referral-based. Eligible seniors can sign up to have a box of nonperishable food delivered to their homes. Contact us at FoodOffice@columbus.gov for information about how to begin referrals.

Go Lunch! Site Supervisor Surveys

A big thank you to all CRPD recreation centers and facilities for another successful year of the Summer Food Service Program. We seek feedback from our site supervisors to guide next year’s program improvements. Please find the survey HERE.

After School Program: After School Meals 

As the recreation after-school programs have commenced, meals from the Children's Hunger Alliance will also begin if they haven't already at your sites. The Food Office has managed all required fire inspections for participation in the CHA after-school program. Should you have any questions regarding the CHA program, please get in touch with Daniel at Dajayi@childrenshungeralliance.org

Thank You

Your continuous effort and commitment significantly impact our community. Let's maintain this momentum and keep up the great work. Here's to another successful month in serving our community with dedication and care.

item.title: Food Bite - July Newsletter
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Go Lunch! Summer Food Service Program

Last month we hosted the Go, Lunch! Kick-Off at Glenwood Pool, where we were joined by Director Bernita Reese, Council Member Nancy Day-Achauer and Mayor’s Office Chief of Staff Elon Simms, all of whom helped distribute meals to the youth in attendance.

As we conclude the first month of our Go, Lunch! summer food service program, we express our sincere gratitude to everyone involved. With your dedication and strong communication, we've had a fantastic start. Let's keep this momentum going!

Important Reminders:

  • Site Review Dates: Compliance officers should have completed the initial visit within the first two weeks of each site's opening. Your compliance officers are there to help you, so if you have any questions, contact them directly upon arrival or contact our food office at foodoffice@columbus.gov.
  • Updates and Changes: Please promptly submit the Site Information Change Request form for any alterations in meal times, start/end dates, meal quantities or contact information.
  • Summer Heat Precautions: June's intense heat wave posed challenges, especially at centers without air conditioning. If your site is affected and requires relocation, please inform us immediately so we can direct meal deliveries appropriately. Contact us via phone at 614-645-3642 or email foodoffice@columbus.gov.

Mobile Produce Markets

July 1 marks the beginning of Compliance Month at Mid-Ohio Food Collective. During this month, Mobile Produce Market sites must fulfill two action items before July 31:

  1. Complete the online Civil Rights Refresher quiz . You will receive a completion certificate; please email your certificate to FoodOffice@columbus.gov.
  2. Download and use the new intake forms and eligibility guidelines effective July 1, 2024. Be sure to use these forms moving forward.

Senior Boxes: For centers participating in the Senior Boxes initiative, please continue promoting this service within your local senior communities. Ensure all necessary information on where seniors can pick up their boxes is readily available. Provide information to senior boxes here. Hydration Reminder: With the summer heat intensifying, it's crucial to remind all volunteers about the importance of staying hydrated. Regular hydration helps maintain focus and energy.

Food Safety: Proper Storing of Food

Emergencies like power outages and natural disasters/ advisories can threaten food safety. Being prepared is essential.

  • Maintain Correct Appliance Temperatures: Keep your refrigerator at or below 40°F (4°C), and your freezer at 0°F (-18°C) to inhibit bacterial growth and keep food safe.
  • Use Appliance Thermometers: Place thermometers in both the refrigerator and freezer to monitor the safety of your food. If the refrigerator temperature exceeds 40°F (4°C) for two hours or more during a power outage, discard the food to prevent foodborne illnesses.

Thank You

Your continuous effort and commitment significantly impact our community. Let's maintain this momentum and keep up the great work. Here's to another successful month in serving our community with dedication and care.

item.title: Food Bite - June Newsletter
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Go Lunch! Summer Food Service Program

We are delighted to celebrate the first month of our eagerly anticipated Go Lunch! Summer Food Service Program. A heartfelt thank you to all centers and site supervisors for providing nourishing meals to the children in your communities.

Important Reminders:

  • Visibility of Materials: Please ensure that yard signs, meal times and menus remain visible throughout the program. This helps keep everyone informed and ensures smooth operations.
  • Meal Ordering: Orders for each day's meals must be placed by 1 p.m. for the next operating day. Please ensure orders for Monday meals are placed by 1 p.m. on Friday.
  • Updates and Changes: Should there be any changes in meal times, start/end dates, meal quantities, or contact information, kindly submit the Site Information Change Request form promptly.

Mobile Produce Markets

Now that we are entering the third month, our Mobile Produce Markets continue to thrive thanks to the efforts of all involved centers. Your dedication ensures community members have access to fresh, delicious produce. We have a couple of suggestions to enhance the effectiveness of these markets further:

  • Rack Cards: To ensure community members are well-informed about where they can access produce, please consider placing rack cards in premade bags or distributing them at the table as individuals pick up their produce. Each center should have received a supply of Rack Cards in their respective mailboxes.
  • Produce Bags: Encourage participants to bring back and reuse their cloth bags for future visits to the Mobile Produce Market. This not only promotes sustainability but also helps maintain an efficient distribution process.

Thank you for your continuous effort and commitment to serving our community. Let's keep up the great work as we move forward with these valuable programs.

Food Safety: Proper Storing of Food

Ensure Proper Food Storage Temperatures and Conditions: Storing food at the right temperature is crucial for preventing the growth of bacteria and ensuring food safety. Here are key practices to ensure proper storage:

  • Maintain the Right Refrigerator and Freezer Temperatures: Keep your refrigerator at or below 40°F (4°C) and the freezer at 0°F (-18°C). These temperatures slow the growth of bacteria and ensure that your food remains safe for extended periods.

item.title: Food Bite - May Newsletter
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Mobile Produce Markets

The Food and Nutrition Office would like to thank all the community centers participating in the Mobile Produce Market program for a successful first month. Please note, start times may vary slightly due to MOFC delivery. The Food and Nutrition Team will continue to provide support at centers.

Each center manages its Mobile Produce Market uniquely, but we would like to offer some tips to enhance efficiency:

  • Volunteers: Every volunteer must be signed in using the Civil Rights Training Log Sheet. To streamline this process, gather volunteers as they arrive at the market and have them sign the sheet.
  • Vehicle Produce Pickup: Consider preparing bags in advance for individuals choosing this option. Assign roles of traffic control, check in and car loading allowing for a smooth and swift service.

Go Lunch! Summer Food Service Program

We are just one month away from the launch of our Summer Food Service Program. As a reminder, each center is required to designate two representatives as Site Supervisors for the duration of the program. Site Supervisor Training Sessions will be held at the Jerry Hammond Center and you can register here.

Food Safety for You

In spirit of spring, let’s go over proper washing and handling of produce that you may find in season:

  • Wash Your Hands
  • Clean Produce Before Storing
  • Use a Produce Brush
  • Dry After Washing
  • Separate from Raw Meats
  • Prep Food Safely
  • Store Food Properly at 40°F

Notable Training Dates

  • FreshTrak Training: With the Mobile Produce Markets well underway, becoming more familiar with the FreshTrak website is highly recommended. A training session is available on May 21, from 2-3:30 p.m. via ZOOM. You can register for the training HERE.
  • Food Safety Level 1: Understanding food safety is crucial, particularly for those involved in food banking. A Food Safety Level 1 training session is scheduled for May 29 from 2-4:30 p.m. via Zoom. Registration is available here..
